title: Seed buckets and stability warmup notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal notebook for a seeded-bucket rollout that focuses on stability priming rather than pure canary correctness checks. Keep lightweight, actionable.

High-level idea:
- Instead of a single tiny canary, create multiple deterministic seed buckets (hash(uid) mod N) and drive small, partially overlapping cohorts through the new model variant to exercise different codepaths and KV/cache states. The goal: exercise cold caches + prefix caching, warm GPU memory patterns, and surface long-tail latency/quality regressions.

Bucket design notes:
- N = 8 seed buckets (0..7), each ~0.5% of traffic => total seeded traffic = 4%.
- Buckets chosen by stable hash of client_id or api_key. Advantage: sticky, easy to reproduce.
- Overlap rule: for first 24h, do NOT move users between buckets to observe per-bucket warming. After 24h allow rehash window for new signups only.
- Control users: keep 1% untouched baseline cohort for golden prompt comparison (static set).

Warmup sequence (per-bucket):
1) Prefix-priming small requests (0.1% of bucket qps) to populate KV cache for common prefixes. Use the top-20 high-frequency prefixes from last 7 days.
2) Gradual ramp within bucket across 3 waves: 10% -> 40% -> 100% of bucket allowance, spacing 15m between steps for load stabilization.
3) Background low-priority batching jobs to exercise long sequences (~1024 tokens) once per bucket during off-peak.
4) Monitor model heat (cache hit rate, KV miss rate) and only proceed to next wave if heat metric shows expected increase.

Telemetry and guardrails (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for token generation + overall response time. Alert threshold: p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.35 or absolute p99 > 3s.
- Error rates: generation_errors and 5xx. Alert if generation_errors rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.
- Quality signals: golden prompt pass-rate drop > 2% absolute or BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity regressions on evaluation harness.
- Semantic regression: hallucination spike measured by hallucination-detector run on sampled responses. Trigger if > 1.5x baseline.
- Cost signal: tokens-per-request jump > 10% (unexpected inflation may indicate prompt drift).
- Cache/kv metrics: prefix cache hit ratio should rise steadily during priming. If it stays flat -> investigate cache key mismatch.

Fallback and routing policies:
- Fast fallback path: if latency or errors cross thresholds, route new traffic to quantized-compat variant (model=vX-quant) while leaving seeded buckets isolated for debugging.
- Hard cutoff: if golden-pass drops > 5% or customer-impacting error rate >1% -> immediate halt for all buckets and initiate rollback runbook.
- Rollforward: if issues isolated to single bucket, evict that bucket by reassigning its users to default routing and continue others.

Preflight checklist (do before seeding):
- [ ] Verify canary harness test coverage for top-10 client intents. Link tests: INF-2345.
- [ ] Smoke test quantized fallback in staging with same weightings.
- [ ] Ensure observability dashboards are live for the buckets (p50/p95/p99, cache hit, golden prompts).
- [ ] Confirm runbook owner and pager on call (cc: @infra-oncall in #deploy-alerts).
- [ ] Confirm dataset of golden prompts and evaluation script availability.

Operational playbook snippets:
- If a bucket shows elevated latency but stable error rate: slow the bucket ramp (hold current wave for additional 30m), increase batching cap to reduce per-token overhead, run hotspot profiler on serving nodes.
- If quality regressions on golden prompts: freeze rollout and run diff evaluation against latest stable checkpoints, collect sample responses (100 per bucket) and tag in ticket.
- If cache miss patterns persist: check for key normalization mismatch (trimming whitespace, lowercasing) between router and runtime.

Notes on experiment design and statistics:
- Use rolling 30m windows for alerting to avoid transient noise.
- For quality checks prefer paired comparisons on identical prompt sets (within-bucket vs baseline) to reduce variance.
- Track per-client impact so we can quickly identify if a small subset of heavy clients drive a bad signal.

Hand-off and documentation links to create after finalizing plan:
- Short confluence checklist page: "Seeded-bucket rollout playbook" (to be created).
- One-page TL;DR for CS & Prod Eng describing how to opt a customer out of buckets.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How long to keep seeded buckets sticky before normalizing? 72h feels safe for cache warming but increases blast radius. Flag for discussion.
- Should we introduce synthetic priming traffic to accelerate cache heat without real user exposure? Pros/cons list needed.
- Metric for prefix cache expected growth: define numeric target (e.g., hit ratio +12% in 24h) so we have a concrete gate.

Quick links and CLI snippets:
- Reassign bucket: curl -XPOST https://internal-router/assign -d '{"api_key": "K", "bucket": 3 }'  (ops-only)
- Fetch bucket sample: python tools/sample_responses.py --bucket 2 --limit 100 --outfile /tmp/b2.json

Personal notes: keep this lightweight. If things get complicated, spin a new doc per incident rather than bloating this one.

End of notebook.
